title: Kinetic energy and net work
target: Connect net work to a change in kinetic energy.
criteria: Calculate kinetic energy with speed squared.
Use net work rather than one force’s work.
Connect the sign of work to a speed change.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg object moves at 4 m/s. What is kinetic energy?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 0.50 kg model puck moves at 8 m/s. What is kinetic energy?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A motor does +45 J on a cart while resistance does −15 J. What changes the cart’s kinetic energy?
options: The total +60 J from adding magnitudes.
cpa.guide: The work-energy theorem uses signed work from all forces.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A cart starts with 22 J of kinetic energy. A pull does +20 J and friction does −8 J. What is final kinetic energy?
cpa.guide: Net work is +12 J; K_final = 22 + 12 = 34 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: For an object of fixed mass, negative net work occurs during a nonzero motion interval. What happens to its speed?
options: Its final speed must be higher.
Its velocity must point opposite the net force throughout.
cpa.guide: Negative net work reduces kinetic energy and hence speed for fixed mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Kinetic energy changes from 35 J to 50 J. Which net-work statement is correct?
options: +15 J; speed increases for unchanged mass.
0 J because energy is conserved overall.
cpa.guide: ΔK = 50 − 35 = +15 J. Conservation includes transfers into this object.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
